title: Pyaasa is a masterpiece and a good starting point to understand why bollywood films are the way they are.

commenti.body:
I have seen pyaasa. True magnum opus of guru dutt. Great songs and great acting. A critique on indian society at the time and a reflection of how society views artist. A good story of a struggling artist and the final song 'yeh duniya agar mil bhi jaye toh kya' captures it all. 

Waheeda shines in the jane kya tune kahi and mehmood in classic sar jo tera chakraye. In the end the guru dutt remained pyaasa, thirsty of the recognition he deserved and then leaving it all when he gets it. It's a good movie worth your time for all cinephiles out there.

Pyaasa is a tremendous film, and a great starting point for Indian cinema, but, if you’re looking to see how Indian Cinema really became what it is today, you have to double feature Pyaasa with another film that is equally important— SHOLAY. If Pyaasa is the Indian Citizen Kane, then Pyaasa is the Indian Jaws.

Well you are right in a way that Pyaasa was a film that used songs to talk about important and meaningful things. Its lyrics writer Sahir Ludhianvi is considered one of the greatest lyricists of all time and also a very admired poet of the Urdu language of his time.

But, you are incorrect about the point you made that "Pyaasa" is the reason Bollywood has songs. Not only Bollywood but almost the whole of Indian Cinema has originated from its theatre culture which is also the same for other countries'cinemas.Much like Japan's theatre style "Kabuki" with its influence on Japanese films,  festivals like "Ram Leela" were and are still celebrated throughout the country by having their stories enacted by actors in a play. But, the main influence was the "Parsi Theatre", these theatres were situated all over India in the early 1900's owned by Parsis (Zoroastrians) , known for their folk-tales with a heavy degree of songs incorporated in it mainly in the language of Urdu,Hindi, Gujrati etc. They even adapted Shakespeare's plays in their own folklore with numerous songs embedded in it. 

When the owners of these theatres migrated to the cinema, they brought with them the same style of storytelling and spectates.

You are right and I know about songs being a carry over from the theatres. Here, I've tried to explain the proper usage of songs in our films to a foreign audience, who are not used to it and have a perception that songs and dances are random, silly and unrelated to the story (which is sadly true for the current crop of trash that bollywood produces). In the post I have expressed Pyaasa as a good "starting point" to understand how songs can carry the film forward, have deep meaning, and sometimes are better than dialogues. I have claimed that Pyaasa can be a "good introduction" to our unique type of cinema.

Hmm, I think you are right and I may have misunderstood your point there. I just wanted to clarify the origin of the presence of  songs in Indian cinema. It is a "good introduction" , and I don't mean to disparate your point, sorry if it seemed that way.

>Sholay is the Indian Jaws.

Not really. The film had an established megastar(Dharmendra) and a rising superstar(Bachchan). Jaws had no big megastars nor a star director.
This film was playing on a projector in my favorite bar last night

I definitely haven’t delved into Indian cinema as much as I want to but so far Pyaasa has been my favorite! Easily one of the best films I’ve seen. I’m grateful for the insight you’ve given here, and saddened by the fact that I don’t know Hindi and wont be able to access the full depth at display! 

Do you have any other recommendations? I think my next Indian movie will be the cloud-capped star

Watch Guru Dutt's other films like Kagaz ke phool. Cloud capped star is by Ritwik Ghatak. He's a bengali(West bengal) director (like Satyajit Ray). The parallel cinema movement originated and was pioneered by bengali filmmakers. So do check out all of them. Satyajit Ray,  Ritwik Ghatak, Mrinal Sen, Bimal Roy, Tapan Sinha, etc.

As for other industries, I'll have to make another post. So stay tuned.
